packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-04 - first reader response (unverified image reading)

Exposure: no proposed identification or reading of this record appeared in my context. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, overview)
- Single narrow vertical strip of parchment (approx. 3 cm wide x 27 cm tall per the scale), black background, colour checker and ruler. Text runs horizontally, upright as displayed.
- The strip preserves only the LEFT edge of a document written in long lines; every line is cut on the right after ca. 1-3 words. One column of prose, ca. 30 lines visible.
- Top: a large calligraphic, flourished initial line (cadel-style capitals, top line "W?L?H?..."), with a very large flourished initial "I"/"J" descending down the left margin from line 2 to about line 14, with knotwork scrolls.
- Script: German-language cursive (Kurrent/Kanzlei hand), brown ink; looks like a chancery document (charter/letter) rather than a book. Lower left margin has a modern pencil shelfmark-type note written vertically ("Stams, StA, Frag. ..." - archival note, not part of text).
- No rubrics, glosses or ruled columns visible. Small holes near lines ~20 and ~29.
- Tentative: a document in German with an ornamental opening; the strip is a binding strip cut from it.

SELECTED SPANS: the whole strip (all lines, left ends only). Everything right of the cut is lost; the lines are fragments of 1-3 words, so no continuous sense is recoverable. Reading order is top to bottom. "-" at right = cut edge.

image-002.jpg (top tile: heading, initial, lines 1-14 of the text)
002-01 [display line, large cadel capitals:] W(?) L h -   (first letter a large flourished capital, read W? or V?; then "L", "h"; the rest cut)
       [left margin: very large flourished initial I/J, its stem running from line 02 to ~line 14; knotwork scrolls left of it]
002-02 (I/J initial) Michael(?), Dab-   (first letter ambiguous U/M; "ichael" clear; comma after)
002-03 willigung des -   (with a hairline mark/hyphen after "des")
002-04 Hannsen(?) Mai-
002-05 auch hiemit a-
002-06 antwort habe-   (final letter may be "e" with superscript or "n")
002-07 racht, an Lie(?) g-   (overline/stroke in the line gap right; "Lie" uncertain, could be "Lig")
002-08 en Valdwerg(?)-   ("Valdwerge"? last letters at the cut)
002-09 wisen genant-   (single n with possible stroke; "genant" or "genan(n)t")
002-10 rietag(?) an Val-   (first letters uncertain; "ertag"/"rtag" possible)
002-11 en Max(?) Kren-   (second word could be "Hax"/"Hans"; capital H/M ambiguous)
002-12 Vnnd Mitan(?)-
002-13 en, an Lauch(?)-   (third word: "Lauch"/"Lench"/"Leuch" possible)
002-14 [only tops of letters visible at bottom edge of tile; read on next tile]

image-003.jpg (middle tile; lines 003-01..03 overlap 002-11..13, not new text)
003-01 = 002-11 (en Max(?) Kren-; here the second word looks more like "Har"/"Max", unresolved)
003-02 = 002-12 (Vnnd Mitan(?)-)
003-03 = 002-13 (en, an Lauch(?)-)
       [bottom of the knotwork initial ends at about line 003-06 in the left margin]
003-04 khauffman(?)-   (long ascender loops in the gap above; last letters "-mant"/"-manb" at the cut)
003-05 Khauffer, sel(?)-   (after "Khauffer" a long-s/f + "l" fragment)
003-06 en, Mar(?) ain-   ("Mar"/"Mor"/"Hor" ambiguous)
003-07 en den Khau-   (abbreviation or i-dot over "u")
003-08 Cammerlannd(?)-   (first letter C/L ambiguous; "-lannd" with a further letter at the cut)
003-09 [.]ein(?) sacher(?),   (worm/hole at line start obscures 1 letter; second word "sacher"/"forcher" uncertain; comma)
003-10 Aufzacher(?), ab-   (first word uncertain; "ab" clear)
003-11 bewalten B-   ("bewaltern"? possible)
003-12 inndemissig(?) -   (long-s ligature; long horizontal stroke under the line to the right; reading of the whole word uncertain)
003-13 ain Ieder(?) Fu-
003-14 Verleichbrief-   (clear; further letter at cut, prob. "e")
003-15 ligennden Z(?)-
003-16 Vo(r?), merbrun(?)-   (unclear second word; "merbrann"? "verbrann"?)
003-17 Vnd Fünffzeh-   (cut at bottom edge? no; "Fünffzeh" clear)

image-004.jpg (bottom tile; lines 004-01..03 overlap 003-15..17)
004-01 = 003-15 (ligennden Z(?)-)
004-02 = 003-16 (Vo(r?), merbrun(?)- ; on this tile the comma after the first word is visible, second word still uncertain)
004-03 = 003-17 (Vnd Fünffzeh-)
004-04 gewort(?) Kü-   (first word "gewort"/"geworet"/"gewert" uncertain; "Kü" or "Rü")
004-05 Khailen, Vnd-   ("Khailen"/"Khailny" ; comma)
004-06 Vnns(er?) vorsch(?)-   (second word uncertain: "vorschl"/"brechl")
004-07 halten, besi(?)g-
004-08 handlen, Khü(?)-
004-09 meiner Erbe-   ("Erb" + letter at cut)
004-10 Mair, Vnnd a-
004-11 Vnnd alls(?) E(?)-   ("alls"/"alle" + capital at cut)
004-12 er meiner -
004-13 Vleissig(?) Pitr(?)-   (long-s pair; reading of second word uncertain)
004-14 Haller gebr(?)-   (last visible line; strip ends just below)
Left margin: modern pencil note written vertically: "Stams, StA, Frg. 60 r(?)" - archival, not text.

END OF FACE 1 (image-001 overview; tiles 002-004). Total distinct text lines on face 1: 1 display line + ca. 34 text lines? (counted: 002-02..13 = 12, 003-04..17 = 14, 004-04..14 = 11 -> 37 text lines).

FACE 2 LAYOUT SURVEY (image-005.jpg, overview)
- Same strip photographed lying horizontally (rotated 90 deg relative to face 1). Appears to be the back (dorse) of the strip.
- Apparently no writing of its own at overview scale: the flourished initial and some line-starts at the left end look like show-through (mirror-image, grey) from face 1. A horizontal fold/crease runs the length; small holes and stains.
- Modern pencil note upper right: "Stams, StA, Frg. 60v" (archival).
- A grey rectangle (masking box, added in imaging) covers part of the lower middle.
- Tiles 006-008 to check for any faint original writing.

image-006.jpg (face 2, left end)
- Only show-through: grey mirror-image of the flourished initial (upper half) and of the display-line capitals (lower left), plus faint grey vertical traces that are the face-1 line starts seen through the membrane. No original ink of its own on this face in this tile; nothing to transcribe.
- Horizontal crease along the middle; small tear/notch at the left edge.

image-007.jpg (face 2, middle; overlaps 006 at the knotwork show-through on the left)
- Show-through of the knotwork terminal of the initial at left; otherwise blank membrane with a lengthwise crease, a cross crease, a hole and brown spots. Grey masking rectangle lower right (imaging mask; whatever lies under it is not visible to me). No original writing seen.

image-008.jpg (face 2, right end; overlaps 007 at the grey mask on the left)
- Modern pencil: "Stams, StA, Frg. 60v" (archival). Faint grey show-through of face-1 line ends; no original writing of its own. Grey mask at lower left (same as in 007).

LIMITATIONS AND SUMMARY
- Face 1 (tiles 002-004): all ca. 37 text lines plus the display line read, but only the first 1-3 words of each line survive (strip cut on the right), so no connected sentence is recoverable; many words uncertain as flagged. German, Kurrent/chancery cursive; spellings with doubled consonants (Vnnd, Hannsen, ligennden), "Kh-" (khauffman, Khauffer, Khailen). Word-content suggests a legal/property document (Verleichbrief, antwort, Kammer?-, Fünffzeh-), observation only.
- Face 2 (tiles 006-008): blank dorse with show-through only; area under the grey imaging mask unseen.
- A wider image of the original document would be needed to read any connected text; nothing further is recoverable from this strip.
- I did not hit the image limit.
